legend: Cut surface of the parotid tumour, showing multiple cystic formations filled with keratin-like material.
Multiple cysts with focal bud-like epithelial outer protrusions and a few solid epithelial cell nests. The cystic spaces contain lamellar keratin material.
The cyst wall is lined by bland stratified squamous epithelium with keratinization through parakeratotic cells. Note the lack of a granular cell layer.

diagnosis: Keratocystoma in the parotid gland of a 17-year-old boy
legend: The tumour consists of haphazardly distributed multiple cysts and scattered solid squamous cell islands. The cystic spaces are filled with keratotic lamellae. The cyst walls are lined by stratified squamous epithelium showing a keratotic surface without a granular cell layer. Each cyst and some solid squamous cell nests are surrounded by collagenous stroma. The squamous epithelial cells have uniform, bland nuclei and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. The solid squamous cell nests are focally located within the parotid gland parenchyma in conjunction with the ducts, but these findings should not be interpreted as invasive growth.
